description:
Canonical vectors for the DIRECTED-destination predicate, shared by two independent implementations: the backends' DIRECTED_DST_PATTERN (meshcom_mock/classifier/types.py, vendored into MCProxy as src/mcapp/classifier/types.py by the classifier subtree — this fixture rides the same subtree, so both backends always replay the copy that sits beside the pattern they compile) and the webapp's isDirectedDst (src/utils/callsignUtils.ts, which composes classifyDst + effectiveDst instead of a regex). A message is DIRECTED when its destination resolves to a personal callsign rather than to a group, a broadcast, or the time channel; it is a property of the ROUTING, never of the message text.

Semantics: resolve the dst to its effective target FIRST (via-routed dst is 'VIA[,VIA2],TARGET' — the target is the last comma component, surrounding whitespace ignored), then the target is directed iff it contains at least one ASCII letter, consists only of [A-Z0-9./-], and is not one of the reserved aliases 'ALL' (broadcast), 'TEST' (group, per group_dst_vectors.json) or 'TIME' (time channel) — all three matched case-INSENSITIVELY. Requiring a letter is what rejects every numeric group id without needing the 1..99999 range test: an out-of-range numeric like '100000' is not a group AND not a person. '*' is rejected by the character class.

HISTORY (2026-07-27): this predicate replaced a bare /^[A-Z0-9]+-\d+$/ that ran only as a classifier CATEGORY rule. That old form had three holes, each pinned by vectors below: it required an SSID (a DM to a bare 'DL1EEN' was never directed), it was anchored against the raw dst (a via-routed DM 'DJ8MEH-82,DJ8MEH-8' was never directed), and — the root cause of the missing DIRECTED badge — 'directed' occupied the single-valued `category` slot, where the priority-90 routing rule lost first-match-wins to any lower-priority CONTENT rule, so a DM whose text merely started with '73' or 'Hello' was classified 'greeting' and silently stopped being directed. Directedness is now ALSO emitted as the `directed` extra_tag, which accumulates independently of the category slot.

SYNC RULE: canonical source is THIS file at mc-chat/meshcom_mock/classifier/directed_dst_vectors.json (mc-chat is the subtree upstream). MCProxy receives it verbatim through `git subtree pull --prefix=src/mcapp/classifier`. The webapp vendors a parse-equal copy at webapp/src/utils/__tests__/directed_dst_vectors.json (Prettier may reformat it; only content drift is a failure). Every repo replays every vector against its own implementation, and sibling drift-checks self-skip when the sibling checkout is absent.

vectors.name: bare callsign, no SSID (old ^[A-Z0-9]+-\d+$ rule missed this)
digit-leading callsign still has a letter
portable suffix stays on the person side
ALLE is not the ALL alias (anchored exclusion)
TESTER is not the TEST group (anchored exclusion)
numeric above the group range is still not a person
via-routed personal dst resolves to its target (old rule missed this)
via-routed group dst is not directed despite the letters in the relay
two relays then a personal target
whitespace around a via-routed target is ignored
a sidebar pair key is never a directed dst
